title: Scalar endomorphisms of the relative dualizing complex over a complete trait
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, put $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, and work on ordinary small-etale $D^+$ with signed Tate twists and ordinary compact-support right adjoints $p^!$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. A trait is $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, where $R$ is a Noetherian local domain of dimension one with principal maximal ideal. Suppose $S$ is complete and strictly henselian (its local ring is henselian and its residue field is separably closed), of mixed characteristic, with $\ell$ invertible. Here henselian means simple roots of monic polynomials over the residue field lift to $R$. Let $p_T:T\to S$ be an integral regular finite-type quasi-projective scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Quasi-projective means admitting a locally closed immersion into some $\mathbf P^N_S$. A regular closed immersion has ideal locally generated by a regular sequence [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. The virtual relative dimension $e_T$ of $p_T$ is $r-c$ in a local factorization as a regular closed immersion of codimension $c$ followed by a smooth morphism of relative dimension $r$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Put $K_T=p_T^!A_S(-e_T)[-2e_T]$.

For every nonempty open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ [def-weil-open-immersion], the scalar-action maps
$$A\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{End}_{D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)}(K_T),\qquad A\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{End}_{D^+(U_{\mathrm{et}},A)}(j^*K_T)$$
are isomorphisms. Under these identifications open restriction is the identity of $A$, so it is injective. The conclusion does not assume punctual purity of $T$, or that its relative Gysin class is invertible.

source.place: Expose XVI, Lemma 3.5.9 proof, printed p.250: scalar endomorphism identification for K_Y before assuming purity of Y, and detection on a nonempty open. Restrict to the complete mixed-characteristic traits of section 3.7.

proof.text:
Write $Q=p_T^!A_S$ before the normalization by $e_T$. Apply constructible trait biduality with $X=T$ and $M=A_T$. Its base hypotheses are exactly those of the item; quasi-projectivity supplies the required compactifiable finite-type structure map. The sheaf $A_T$ is constructible: the single stratum $T$ carries the constant finite rank-one module. The unit isomorphism $R\mathcal Hom_A(A_T,Q)=Q$ identifies $\eta_{A_T}$ with
$$s_Q:A_T\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_A(Q,Q).$$
Indeed, on sections the evaluation $R\mathcal Hom_A(A_T,Q)\otimes_A^L A_T\to Q$ is $q\otimes a\mapsto aq$; transposing after symmetry sends $a$ to $q\mapsto aq$. Thus this is the scalar-action map, rather than an unspecified isomorphism of objects. This application uses no pinnings or purity assertion about $T$.

source.place: XVI, Lemma 3.5.9 proof, p.250, local-biduality sentence; explicit evaluation-transpose calculation

proof.text:
Put $L=A_T(-e_T)[-2e_T]$, so $K_T=Q\otimes_A^L L$. The signed finite twists are locally free of rank one with evaluation identifications. Consequently $L$ has tensor inverse $L^{-1}=A_T(e_T)[2e_T]$: locally the line and its dual evaluate to $A_T$, and the opposite shifts cancel. Tensoring by $L$ is therefore an equivalence with inverse tensoring by $L^{-1}$. For every test object $P$, tensor--Hom adjunction and this inverse give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(P,R\mathcal Hom_A(Q\otimes L,Q\otimes L))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P\otimes Q,Q)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P,R\mathcal Hom_A(Q,Q)).$$
The Yoneda full-faithfulness bijection turns this natural Hom isomorphism and its inverse into inverse morphisms of the two internal-Hom objects (their composites are identities by faithfulness). It sends $s_{K_T}$ to $s_Q$, since tensoring carries $a\,1_Q$ to $a\,1_{Q\otimes L}$. Thus $s_{K_T}:A_T\to R\mathcal Hom_A(K_T,K_T)$ is an isomorphism. The even shifts introduce no scalar sign.

source.place: Tag 08J9, lemma-internal-hom; cancellation of the finite rank-one twist and opposite shifts

proof.text:
An open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ is an etale object of $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, and its slice site is $U_{\mathrm{et}}$. Restriction of derived internal Hom to this slice gives
$$j^*R\mathcal Hom_A(K_T,K_T)\cong R\mathcal Hom_A(j^*K_T,j^*K_T).$$
Restrict $s_{K_T}$ through this isomorphism. The result is exactly $s_{j^*K_T}$: evaluation and tensor restriction send multiplication by a local coefficient section to multiplication by its restriction. In particular it is an isomorphism $A_U\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_A(j^*K_T,j^*K_T)$. This argument concerns restriction on the source scheme and does not assume a base-change isomorphism for $p_T^!$.

source.place: Tag 08JB, lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U; topologies.tex small-etale slice localization

proof.text:
For $V=T$ with $C=K_T$, and for $V=U$ with $C=j^*K_T$, take degree-zero derived global sections of $s_C$. The global internal-Hom formula identifies
$$\operatorname{End}_{D(V_{\mathrm{et}},A)}(C)=H^0(V,R\mathcal Hom_A(C,C))\cong H^0(V,A_V)=\Gamma(V,A_V).$$
For the last equality, the category of module sheaves is Grothendieck, hence has enough injectives. Take an injective resolution of $A_V$ zero in negative degrees. It is K-injective; global sections is left exact because it is $\operatorname{Hom}(A_V,-)$. The degree-zero injective-resolution comparison therefore identifies $H^0(V,A_V)$ with $\Gamma(V,A_V)$. Under the displayed map a section acts on $C$ by multiplication, by the evaluation description in Step 1. Thus this is a bijection induced by scalar action; it preserves identity, addition and composition since multiplication of coefficients does. The bounded-below derived categories are full subcategories of these ambient derived categories, so the displayed endomorphisms are the requested ones.

source.place: Tag 08JA, lemma-section-RHom-over-U; derived.tex Tags 013K, 05TD and 070J for the degree-zero calculation

proof.text: The underlying space of the integral scheme $T$ is nonempty and irreducible. Every nonempty open $U$ of an irreducible space is irreducible: two nonempty relatively open subsets are nonempty opens of $T$ and therefore intersect. Both $T$ and $U$ are consequently connected. The constant-module locally-constant model identifies $\Gamma(V,A_V)$ with locally constant functions $|V|\to A$. Such a function on a nonempty connected space is constant: each fibre is open and its complement is the union of the other open fibres, so two inhabited fibres would disconnect the space. Its constant value is unique by nonemptiness. For both $V=T,U$, Step 4 therefore identifies the actual map $a\mapsto a\,1_C$ with an isomorphism from $A$. Finally $j^*(a\,1_{K_T})=a\,1_{j^*K_T}$, since module inverse image restricts the scalar action. Thus open restriction is the identity of $A$ under these two scalar-action isomorphisms, and is injective.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q93-7c828637d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the source: ILO XVI 3.5.4–3.5.10, pp.248–250. Lemma 3.5.9 gets Λ≅End(K_Y) from 'bidualité locale', which it cites to SGA 4½ Th. finitude 4.3, and then detects the claim on a nonempty open. The item states exactly that sentence; its statement is byte-identical to the base copy, and only the unused def-weil-proper-morphism stmt_dep was dropped, which is correct. The new node lem-per-complete-trait-constructible-biduality is unsplit, statement-only and self-contained. It is a true special case of Deligne's biduality over a regular base of dimension ≤1, checked on X=S, X=s (Q=A(−1)[−2]) and X=η. Quasi-projectivity gives the compactification that thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint needs. It does not duplicate an existing node. The gabber-local-duality-general, potential-local-duality, potential-dualizing-finite-pullback, potential-dualizing-regular-unit and absolute-gysin-purity nodes all already contain this item in their dependency closure, so citing them would be circular (C6). The finite-residue, etale-geometric and fix-general biduality nodes work over field bases, and lem-per-coefficient-change-dualizing assumes a dualizing complex. The new node is also not a restated clause of the item: it says nothing about End or open restriction. All five steps are correct against the cited statements, which I read. Step 1 is biduality for A_T, whose evaluation transpose is the scalar map. Step 2 cancels the twist using the signed rank-one twists, closed adjunction and Yoneda, with even shifts. Step 3 restricts RHom to the slice, as in Stacks 08JB. Step 4 passes to global sections with Stacks 08JA and the degree-0 injective resolution. Step 5 uses that U is connected because T is irreducible, together with the locally constant model of A_V (Stacks 03P5). The 8 tool_uses are generic and I accept them. Advisory: identifying j^* with restriction to the slice follows the DAG's standing convention. Maintainer note: the split of the new node must avoid both SGA 4½, because of the route lock, and the potential-dualizing package, because of the cycle.
